compliance.title: Compliance
compliance.hint: Which rules MDARJ checks your company against.
compliance.lawModeOn: On: overtime uses the law's multipliers, the leave types the law requires are created, the optional disability field appears on employees, and the compliance check reads the law.
compliance.lawModeOff: Off: only your own company rules below are checked.
compliance.rulesPlaceholder: e.g. Friday prayer break is 30 minutes. Uniform is required on every shift.
compliance.rulesHint: Written in your own words. The compliance check reads them exactly as written.

workWeek.title: Work week
workWeek.hint: Pick the weekly rest days. A change starts on the date you choose and never changes earlier days or approved payrolls.
workWeek.setupHint: Pick the weekly rest days. You can change them later in Settings, from any date you choose.
workWeek.summary: Rest: {rest} · {working, plural, one {# working day} other {# working days}} a week

payroll.title: Payroll rules
payroll.hint: How pay, deductions and overtime are worked out. Changes start on the date you choose.
payroll.setupHint: How pay, deductions and overtime are worked out. MDARJ's defaults follow common practice in Egypt; change only what your company does differently.

divisor.working_days: Salary ÷ working days of the month

payroll.divisorHint: Hourly rate = daily rate ÷ the shift hours (without unpaid break).

lateness.exactHint: Every late minute is deducted at the hourly rate. Simplest choice.
lateness.tieredHint: Fixed amounts by how late: e.g. 16–60 min late = ¼ day.

payroll.capHint: Either way, one day's lateness and early-leave deduction never exceeds one day's pay.
payroll.overtimeHint: Overtime pay = hours × hourly rate × the multiplier. Arriving early is not overtime.

checkIn.ipsEmpty: None: people can check in from anywhere.
checkIn.ipsSet: Check-in is accepted only from these addresses or ranges.

Setup.intro: A few minutes now saves work later: pay, attendance and leave all read these settings. Skip anything you are not sure about and finish it later in Settings.

LawRef.title: Labor Law No. 14 of 2025
LawRef.description: Reference values the compliance check will use (EG-LABOR v1). A labor lawyer must confirm them before launch.
LawRef.eg03Value: At least 1 hour a day; no more than 5 hours in a row
LawRef.eg04Value: At least 24 hours in a row, fully paid
LawRef.eg05Value: 15 days in year 1, 21 from year 2, 30 after 10 years or age 50
LawRef.eg13Value: Day +35%, night +70%, rest day double pay
